newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy and India discuss nuclear test ban treaty.
newsitem.headline: Italy and India discuss nuclear test ban treaty.

text.p: A nuclear test ban treaty which India is refusing to sign was discussed on Tuesday at talks between Italian Prime Minister Romani Prodi and Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma, the Italian government said.

An official statement said the treaty and a "common interest" in reform of the United Nations Security Council were among international issues Prodi discussed with Sharma, who is on an official visit to Italy.
The test ban treaty, which would end all nuclear explosions, has already been signed by 124 states including Italy.
India is among 44 nations with nuclear power whose signing and ratification are needed for the treaty to come into force.
India has vowed never to sign what it calls an unequal treaty unless the atomic powers devise a timetable for destroying their nuclear arsenals.
The statement gave no details of the discussions between Prodi and Sharma on the treaty.

It said the two men had reviewed growing bilateral economic and commercial links. Bilateral trade was worth almost four trillion lire ($2.6 billion) in 1995, an increase of 43 percent on 1994, the statement said.
